---
title: Items and types
description: An item is one thing a person keeps, such as a photo or a contact, and its type says which properties it holds.
job: A builder learns how an item's type decides what the item holds and where that type comes from.
kind: concept
---

Marfa **holds every item to its type**. Every item has fixed fields: `id`, `state`, `version` and its three timestamps ([Items](/catalog/items)).

## What a type does

This photo lacks the `blob_ref` and `mime_type` that `core.file` requires, so it is refused with `400 invalid_properties`:

```http title="Request"
POST /items
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "type": "core.file.image", "properties": { "title": "Kitchen before the move" } }
```

**A property the type doesn't declare is kept**, unless [`strict_mode`](/reference/instance-settings#enforcement-levers) names the type.

A **description** says in one sentence what the type is for. **Guidance** is optional Markdown for an agent or an app builder. An `app` type takes none. [Type definition](/catalog/type-definition#descriptions-and-guidance) has who may write them, their lengths and the [display hints](/catalog/type-definition#display-hints). [Define a type](/build/define-a-type) adds one.

### Building on another type

`core.file.image` adds `width` and `height` to its parent file. **A listing includes the types beneath it that aren't hidden.** A child can't reshape an inherited property ([Type definition](/catalog/type-definition#parent-and-inheritance)).

<TypeInheritance />

## Who adds types where

The first segment of a type's ID is its **namespace** ([Type definition](/catalog/type-definition#identifier)).

| Namespace | Example | Who adds types |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `core`, `system` and `marfa` | `core.note`, `system.view` | Marfa. No one replaces a shipped type. |
| `common` | `common.ticket` | Only by installing a [Marfa plugin](/use/install-a-plugin). |
| `app` | `app.readinglist.entry` | An app, for its own machinery. |
| `user` | `user.recipe` | The owner, or any credential with write on `user.*`. |
| Any other root | `acme.deal` | A credential whose type map grants the write. |

A Marfa plugin may also use a root of its own, such as `rss` for the RSS connector's types.

The first `app.<vendor>` type's app owns that vendor, and its sign-in reaches it with no scope naming it ([Access](/build/access#an-apps-own-types)). The owner can [give that data away or delete it](/use/manage-app-data).

Items under `system` or `app` are **hidden**. Listings, searches and counts omit them unless the request names that type exactly or passes `include=hidden`, and a view never lists them. The bin lists an `app` item. A `system` item is revoked, never binned.

## What an item holds

| Kind | Holds | Shape set by | Moves the version |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Properties | What the item is | The type | Yes |
| Tags | Labels, such as `paperwork` | No one | No |
| Extensions | One app's JSON | That app | No |

Tags and extensions are the item's **metadata**, not a key's metadata map ([Access](/build/access#what-a-credential-reaches)).

### Properties

[Update an item](/reference/api/items/updateItem) sends the properties that changed. **A null leaves an optional or undeclared property as it stands**, and is refused on a required one. `clear_properties` removes each name it lists, but not a required property. `properties_mode: replace` writes the whole set and omits a null.

### Tags

[Add](/reference/api/metadata/addItemTags) and [remove](/reference/api/metadata/removeItemTag) name the `version` you read. [Replace](/reference/api/metadata/replaceItemTags) names the tags you read as `read_tags`. A mismatch is `409 version_conflict`. **A tag write leaves the version alone** and needs write on the type. A filter keeps items with every named tag. [Limits](/use/limits) gives the sizes.

### Extensions

An extension is JSON under a namespace, such as `app.ledger.reminders`. [Replace an extension namespace](/reference/api/extensions/replaceItemExtension) replaces that one. A key reaches it only when its extension map names it, and needs write on the type. A missing namespace answers `document: null`. A stale `read_revision` is `409 version_conflict`. Tag and extension writes announce `metadata.changed` ([Events](/build/events)).

## Where an item came from

**Source** names what wrote the item, and it never changes. With `source_id`, the pair is the item's **natural key**: the same pair, for the same type, updates that item.

### Library and feed

The **library** is what a person chose to keep. The **feed** is what arrives in volume. A type's feed window moves an active feed item to the bin and leaves library items alone.

`read_only: true` means a connector run will overwrite it. **That is advice, not a lock** ([Connectors](/build/connectors)).

## An item's life

An item starts `active`. **Archiving** hides it from a listing that names no state. A read by `id` still answers it.

<ItemLifecycle />

A move leaves the [version](/build/versions) alone, so [a transition](/reference/api/items/transitionItem) can name the state you read as `from`. **If the item has left it, nothing moves** (`409 state_conflict`).

### Delete and purge

**A delete is a soft delete** into the bin, which the API calls the trash. It takes the items a cascading edge reaches, and the item's [parts](/build/edges#parts).

**Purging** deletes a binned item, with its edges and parts. It needs `items.purge` and write on the type. Housekeeping purges items kept past [`trash_retention_days`](/use/limits).

The [items](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/items.md) and [types](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/types.md) chapters are the rules.
